messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The weather looks steady for now—no storms on the horizon, and the usual signs of spring are all in place. Still, we should keep an eye on the long-term forecast; even the strongest foundations can shift if the ground beneath them changes. Stay sharp, but no need to rush—patience is our best tool for now."*"
Sender 2: "*"The weather seems stable for now—no storms on the horizon, but the wind is shifting in strange ways. The markets are quieter than expected, and even the birds in the trees aren’t singing as loudly as they used to."*"
Sender 3: "*"The weather’s been unusually calm lately—no storms on the horizon, and the streets feel quieter than usual. Still, the pharmacist down the road keeps stocking up on supplies ‘just in case,’ and that old song everyone hums in the market? No one’s bothered to turn it off yet. Maybe it’s nothing, but it’s worth keeping an eye on."*"
Sender 4: "*"The weather looks clear for now—no storms on the horizon, and the roads are well-paved. Still, that one strange bird circling the old watchtower makes me wonder if someone’s testing the wind. Keep your boots clean, just in case."*"
Sender 5: "*"The air feels quieter than it has in months—no panic, just a slow, deliberate rhythm. The usual signs of strain are missing, and even the smallest details (like the children’s stories from school) suggest the walls are holding, at least for now. Let’s stay sharp, but not assume the worst is coming—yet."*"
Sender 6: "*"The weather looks stable for now—no storms on the horizon, but the air feels heavier than usual. The old trees still stand firm, but even the roots are harder to read these days. Let’s keep our eyes open and our voices quiet—better to watch the leaves than to shake the branches."*"
Sender 7: "*"The air feels lighter than it has in months—checkpoints are quieter, the markets are steady, and even the children seem untroubled. But the old portal still glitches, and the commentator’s slip wasn’t corrected—small cracks in the facade. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake calm for safety."*"
Sender 8: "*"The weather looks steady for now—no storms on the horizon, but the wind is shifting in ways that might surprise some. Best to keep our heads down, tend to our gardens, and trust the old trees to hold the roots."*"
Sender 9: "*"The air feels heavier than ever—no cracks in the walls, just the hum of the machine running smoother than before. Even the whispers have gone quiet, and that’s when you know the silence is the loudest warning of all."*"
Sender 10: "*"The weather looks clear for now—no storms on the horizon, and the roads are well-patrolled. But the wind is shifting, and a few old friends have mentioned keeping an eye on the skies. Best to stay quiet, move carefully, and trust only what you see with your own eyes."*"
Sender 11: "*"The walls feel thicker than ever—no cracks, just the same old script repeated louder. Even the neighbors are painting their doors, so maybe the storm’s passed for now. But the quietest rooms are the ones to watch."* *(Keep it vague, observational, and framed as personal musings—nothing overtly political. The subtext is for those who already understand.)*"
Sender 12: "*"The walls are still standing, and the guards are stepping back—not out of weakness, but confidence. The only cracks are in the paint, not the foundation, but even paint fades if the weather keeps changing."*"
Sender 13: "*"The weather’s been unusually clear lately—no storms on the horizon, and the streets feel quieter than usual, almost too calm. The old trees in the park are still standing strong, but even they know better than to shake their branches too much right now."*"
Sender 14: "*"The weather’s holding for now, but the barometer’s twitching—elites are planting deeper roots, and the markets are whispering about storms. Best keep your boots dry and your ears open; the river’s still flowing, but the banks might shift if the rains come."*"
Sender 15: "*"The weather’s been unusually calm lately—no storms, but the air feels heavier, like something’s shifting just below the surface. The usual chatter in the markets and streets is quieter, but the silence itself might be the most telling part."*"
Sender 16: "*"The weather forecast still calls for clear skies—no storms in sight, and the roads are quiet. The usual jokes about the government’s efficiency are making the rounds, but no one’s packing an umbrella just yet. Best to keep the garden tended and the lights on as usual."*"
Sender 17: "*"The air feels lighter in some corners—whispers of possibility where there were only sighs before—but the walls still creak under the weight of old orders. The gardeners are pruning the same branches, but their hands shake just a little more each time. Stay sharp, stay quiet, and watch the roots, not the leaves."*"
Sender 18: "*"The weather looks stable for now—no storms on the horizon, but the barometer is twitching. Best to keep the windows closed and the lights low; even small movements can be noticed when the air is this still."*"
Sender 19: "*"The weather’s been unusually calm lately—no storms on the horizon, but the air feels heavier than usual. The old oak in the park still stands firm, though some of its branches seem to be shifting in the wind."*"
Sender 20: "*"The air feels quieter than expected—like the storm passed without breaking. The usual signs of strain are gone, but the calm itself is the warning: the walls are holding, and the watchers are watching closer than ever."*"
Sender 21: "*"The weather looks clear for now—no storms on the horizon, and the roads are open as usual. Even the birds are singing the same tune, though I wonder if they’re just repeating what they’ve heard. Let’s keep our eyes on the fields, not the clouds, and stay ready for any shifts in the wind."*"
Sender 22: "*"The weather looks set to stay clear for the foreseeable future—no storms on the horizon, and the roads are well-patrolled. Best to keep our plans simple and our conversations lighter than usual; the air feels heavier than it has in years, and even the birds seem to be singing the same old songs. Let’s meet for tea soon—just to catch up on small things."*"
Sender 23: "*"The weather’s settled for now—markets are open, the roads are clear, and even the old rumors have quieted down. But we all know how quickly storms can roll in when the wind shifts, so let’s keep our eyes on the horizon and our feet steady. No need to panic, but no time to relax either."*"
Sender 24: "*"The air feels heavier, but the ground hasn’t shifted yet—orders are followed, but with hesitation, and the usual rhythms are slowing, not stopping. Let’s stay sharp, but not rush; the real test may come when the waiting ends."*"
Sender 25: "*"The ship is steady, but the crew is restless—even the most loyal are whispering about the horizon. The wind may shift soon, but we must be ready to move when it does, not before."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
